title: Sing, O barren
summary: The passage introduces what is written as something that shall come to pass. The Lord calls on the barren to sing and says the desolate have more children than the married wife.

explicit_facts.text: The passage introduces something written that shall come to pass without identifying the speaker of the introduction.
The Lord calls on the barren to sing and cry aloud.
The Lord says the children of the desolate are more numerous than the children of the married wife.

unspecified_visual_details: No setting or visible appearance of the Lord is described.
The poetic address does not establish a visibly present woman.

spoken_dialogue.text: Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: And then shall that which is written come to pass:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The barren and desolate language is a poetic address, not a narrated birth.
The supplied verse does not identify the speaker of the introductory clause; do not attribute it to Mormon.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict childbirth, a visibly present addressee, or an invented appearance of the Lord.
Do not turn the poetic comparison into a literal gathering of women and children.

title: Enlarge the tent
summary: The Lord commands the addressed one to enlarge her tent and promises that her seed will spread and make desolate cities inhabited.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commands the addressed one to enlarge her tent, stretch its curtains, lengthen its cords, and strengthen its stakes.
The Lord says her seed will spread to the right and left, inherit the Gentiles, and make desolate cities inhabited.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A tent with extended curtains, cords, and stakes can illustrate the metaphor.
unspecified_visual_details: The passage does not narrate a specific tent, family, migration, or city as visibly present.

narration.text: Enlarge the place of thy tent
thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The tent and seed imagery belongs to the prophetic address.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific family, settlement, or migration as an event.

title: Fear not
summary: The Lord promises the addressed one will not be ashamed and identifies himself as her maker and Redeemer.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord tells the addressed one not to fear or be ashamed, and says she will forget the reproach of her youth and widowhood.
The Lord identifies himself as maker, husband, Lord of Hosts, Redeemer, Holy One of Israel, and God of the whole earth.
The Lord says he called her as a forsaken, grieved woman and a refused wife of youth.

unspecified_visual_details: No woman or divine figure is explicitly described as visibly present.

narration.text: Fear not, for thou shalt not be ashamed

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The woman and marriage language functions as poetic address.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal marriage, widowhood, or an appearance of the Lord.

title: Mercy and gathering
summary: The Lord says he forsook the addressed one briefly, but will gather her with great mercies and have everlasting kindness.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he briefly forsook the addressed one but will gather her with great mercies.
The Lord says he hid his face briefly but will have mercy with everlasting kindness.

unspecified_visual_details: No present act of gathering or visible face-hiding is described.

narration.text: with great mercies will I gather thee

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The language is divine reassurance, not a separate narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal abandonment or gathering.

title: A covenant of peace
summary: The Lord compares his oath to the waters of Noah and promises that his kindness and covenant of peace will remain.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord compares his oath not to be wroth with the waters of Noah not going over the earth.
The Lord says that even if mountains depart and hills are removed, his kindness and covenant of peace will remain.

unspecified_visual_details: No flood or moving mountains are narrated as happening now.

narration.text: neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The waters of Noah and departing mountains are comparisons or poetic imagery.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a new flood or mountains physically departing.

title: Stones of beauty
summary: The Lord promises the afflicted one a structure with fair-colored stones, sapphire foundations, agate windows, carbuncle gates, and pleasant-stone borders.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord promises fair-colored stones and foundations of sapphires for the afflicted one.
The Lord promises agate windows, carbuncle gates, and borders of pleasant stones.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic architectural rendering can convey the promised materials.
unspecified_visual_details: The structure's form and its construction are unspecified.

narration.text: I will lay thy stones with fair colors

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses are a promise; they do not narrate construction taking place.
prohibited_inventions: Do not present a completed building or construction as a narrated event.

title: Peace for the children
summary: The Lord promises that the children will be taught by him and have peace, and that the addressed one will be established in righteousness and far from oppression and terror.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says all the addressed one's children will be taught of the Lord and have great peace.
The Lord promises the addressed one will be established in righteousness and far from oppression and terror.

unspecified_visual_details: No children or teaching scene is narrated as visibly present.

narration.text: great shall be the peace of thy children

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The children and their instruction appear in a promise, not a narrated scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent particular children or a specific lesson.

title: Those gathered against thee
summary: The Lord says those who gather against the addressed one do so not by him and will fall for her sake.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says those who gather against the addressed one do not do so by him and will fall for her sake.

unspecified_visual_details: No attackers or battle are explicitly described as visibly present.

narration.text: whosoever shall gather together against thee shall fall

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a promise, not an account of a battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict attackers or a battle as present.

title: The smith and the waster
summary: The Lord describes creating a smith who works at coals and makes an instrument, and creating the waster to destroy.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he created a smith who blows coals in a fire and brings forth an instrument for his work.
The Lord says he created the waster to destroy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic depiction may show the stated smith, coals, and work instrument.
unspecified_visual_details: The smith's identity and appearance, the instrument's form, and any destruction are unspecified.

narration.text: the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes creation and roles; it does not narrate destruction occurring now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the smith's identity, an instrument design, or a destructive event.

title: No weapon shall prosper
summary: The Lord promises that weapons formed against the addressed one will not prosper and says the heritage of his servants is from him.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says no weapon formed against the addressed one will prosper and she will condemn every reviling tongue in judgment.
The Lord says this is the heritage of his servants and their righteousness is of him.

unspecified_visual_details: No weapon, judgment proceeding, or visible speaker is described as present.

narration.text: No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The weapons and reviling tongues are part of the prophetic assurance; no combat or trial is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or specific judgment scene.
